subject: Nimbus Health — infrastructure demarcation & private/dedicated boundary walkthrough
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@nimbushealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-ops@nimbushealth.com, Thomas Lee <tlee@cloudprocure.io>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: infra demarcation for Private + Dedicated options

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Nimbus is actively evaluating Redwood for a private deployment (HIPAA scope) with a Dedicated fallback for burst traffic. Our security team needs a compact, supplier-friendly packet describing the network demarcation lines between Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) and Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) so we can finish our SIG and CAIQ responses.

Specifically we need: 
- A single-page diagram showing the data/control plane boundaries for both Private and Dedicated.
- A short table of egress/ingress assertions (what leaves customer VPC, what Redwood manages).
- Notes on key controls: KMS scope, audit log surface, and how tenant traffic is isolated on the serving runtime.

Can you share a draft by EOD PT tomorrow? If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough after you send it.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Sr. Security Engineer — Nimbus Health
Aisha.k@nimbushealth.com

[Attachment: Nimbus-SIG-sample-request.pdf (PDF)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, Thomas Lee <tlee@cloudprocure.io>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: infra demarcation for Private + Dedicated options

Hi Aisha — appreciate the clear asks. Draft attached: "nimbus-network-demarcation-v1.pdf" (single-page diagram + short assertions). I also included a control matrix spreadsheet that maps the diagram regions to SOC 2/SIG control owners.

Quick notes up front (high level):
- Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem): control plane traffic (management, telemetry) is carried over an encrypted channel terminated at the customer boundary unless the customer elects Redwood-managed control plane; data plane inference kernels execute in customer-owned subnets or air-gapped enclaves depending on the offering.
- Dedicated (Redwood reserved capacity): customer inference requests route to dedicated GPU pools we manage; network egress is restricted via per-tenant NAT gateways and strict egress ACLs. KV/cache prefixes are logically tenant-scoped and never cross tenant pools.
- KMS: optional customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; in Dedicated we offer CMEK with key policies scoped per-tenant.

Kimberly/Karthik/Priyo — I put you all on CC for a quick redline pass (esp. the egress bullets and KMS wording). Aisha — I propose a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT to walk through the diagram and the supporting RACI. Does that work?

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: nimbus-network-demarcation-v1.pdf, redwood-control-matrix-nimbus.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, Aisha Khan <aisha.k@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: infra demarcation for Private + Dedicated options

Folks — quick edits and clarifications from security: 

1) Egress statements: please change "per-tenant NAT gateways" to "per-tenant controlled egress path (NAT or Egress Gateway), policy enforced via cloud-native FW and Redwood ACLs" — some customers use egress gateways for inspection.

2) KV/cache isolation: add explicit sentence: "All KV caches are encrypted at rest and split by tenant ID; cache shards are pinned to tenant-bound pools where applicable."

3) Control plane telemetry: we only send aggregated, non-PII usage metrics to the Redwood control plane by default for hosted management. For Private with customer-managed control plane we ship logs to customer logging endpoints only.

4) Please attach the annotated SVG layer that show the routing hops (Private control plane hop vs Dedicated data path) — that'll help Nimbus sign off quickly.

I made these as comments in the control matrix (redwood-control-matrix-nimbus.xlsx). Karthik/Priyo — Karthik please confirm the KMS paragraph below, Priyo please confirm the suggested diagram layer attachment.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Architecture — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

[Attachment: private-deploy-annotated-diagram.svg (SVG)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, Thomas Lee <tlee@cloudprocure.io>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: infra demarcation for Private + Dedicated options

Aisha — attached is the updated packet including Kimberly's redlines and the annotated SVG (private-deploy-annotated-diagram.svg).

New items added: 
- Short "acceptance checklist" for Nimbus security reviewers (3 items: verify KMS policy scope, confirm log collection endpoint, confirm egress inspection placement).
- A concise note on rollback/fallback: if Dedicated capacity fails over, traffic is routed via a pre-agreed failover route and request-level fallbacks can be configured to keep inference online with degraded SLA.

Confirmed the 30-min walkthrough tomorrow at 10:00 PT with Thomas on the line — I'll send a calendar invite now. Expected deliverables after call: final diagram (PDF + SVG), signed control matrix, and a scoped SOC 2 statement excerpt we can include in your SIG answers.

Best,
Camila

[Attachments: nimbus-network-demarcation-v1.pdf, redwood-control-matrix-nimbus.xlsx, private-deploy-annotated-diagram.svg]
